note: Majority: null. The Muluki Civil Code 2074 (2017) was sought on the Nepal Law Commission's site (lawcommission.gov.np), whose act indexes load by script and gave no link to it in the pages fetched; not read. Work: the Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act 2056 (2000), Act No. 1 of 2057 B.S., authenticated 21 June 2000 (FAOLEX's copy of the English text): s. 2(a) a child is a minor not having completed sixteen; s. 3(1) no child under 14 shall be engaged in work as a labourer; s. 3(2) no child in the risky work in its schedule; s. 9 no work from 6 p.m. to 6 a.m. and at most six hours a day and 36 a week, which the form doesn't hold. The Labour Act 2074 (2017), Act No. 14 of 2017 (FAOLEX's copy bearing the Law Commission's header), s. 5: no person shall employ a child in any work contrary to law. So general employment from 14, with limits to 16. Whether later amendments changed the Child Labour Act's ages was not read. Performers: neither Act makes an exception for performing, so the form holds barred (my reading of their silence). Service: null. No defence law or ministry page was read (moless.gov.np didn't answer).

sources.title: Child Labor (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 2056 (2000), English text (FAOLEX)
sources.said: "Child" means a minor not having completed the age of sixteen years. ... No child having not attained the age of 14 years shall be engaged in works as a laborer.

sources.title: Labour Act, 2074 (2017), Act No. 14 of 2017, English text (Nepal Law Commission, via FAOLEX)
sources.said: Prohibition on employment of children: No person shall so employ a child in any work as to be contrary to law.
